Bu yüzden bütün şirketlerin özsermaye kârlılığı yıl sonu tüketici enflasyonuyla düzeltildi: 2021 için %4,8, 2022 için %6,3, 2023 için %3,4, 2024 için %1,8, 2025 için %2,4. data_notes: Fiyat, piyasa değeri, F/K ve PD/DD: TradingView tarayıcısı, 13 Kasım 2026. Evren 2.440 paydır: 609'u Toronto Borsası'nda (TSX), 1.249'u TSX Venture'da, 565'i CSE'de, 17'si Cboe Canada'da. Borsa yatırım fonları ve depo sertifikaları evrende yoktur; evrendeki 52 gayrimenkul ve yatırım ortaklığı 1. surda dışarıda kalır.

Evrendeki şirketlerin 1.527'si son 12 ayda zararda; çoğu TSX Venture ve CSE'deki küçük maden arama şirketleri. Bu bir veri eksiği değil: TMX'in Ağustos 2026 raporuna göre TSX Venture'daki 1.496 şirketin %59'u madenci. Kaynağın 'zarar' dediği on şirket ikinci kaynakla karşılaştırıldı; onu da zararda. Piyasa değeri 80 milyon Kanada dolarının üstündeki 772 şirketin %51'inde F/K var.

Karşılaştırma: TMX'in Ağustos 2026 raporuna göre TSX'te fonlar ve depo sertifikaları dışında 667 şirket (evrende 609, %9 az), TSX Venture'da 1.496 şirket (evrende 1.249, %17 az) var. CSE, 30 Eylül 2026'da 739 kote menkul kıymet bildiriyor (evrende 565; CSE şirket değil menkul kıymet sayar). Toplamda evren bu sayıların %16 altında; fark en çok işlem görmeyen küçük paylardan geliyor. Fark %15'in üstünde olduğu için ülke, öbür denetimler tuttuğundan, bu notla yayımlandı.

Denetim (14 Kasım 2026): Royal Bank, TD, Bank of Montreal, Scotiabank ve Enbridge'de fiyat ikinci kaynakla %1 içinde, piyasa değeri %4 içinde, F/K %1 içinde tutuyor; dört bankanın PD/DD'si kendi üçüncü çeyrek raporlarındaki hisse başına defter değeriyle aynı. Toplayıcının hesapladığı F/K, Canadian Net REIT'te 9,11 (şirketin açıkladığı kârla 9,10). PD/DD, Brookfield Business Corporation'da 1,096 (30 Eylül 2026 özsermayesiyle 1,08), Computer Modelling Group'ta 5,85 (30 Eylül 2026 özsermayesiyle 5,74; oran sayfasındaki 3,8 pay geri alımından önceki özsermayeye dayanıyor).

Şirketin belgesiyle düzeltilenler (14 Kasım 2026). Brookfield Wealth Solutions: toplayıcının hesapladığı F/K (30,9) ikinci kaynakla tutmadı. Pay, Brookfield Corporation payıyla değiştirilebilen A sınıfı paydır ve kârın çok küçük bölümü bu sınıfa düşer; F/K ölçülemediği için boş bırakıldı ve şirket 'kâr verisi eksik' görünür. StrikePoint Gold'un PD/DD'si (5,4) doğrulanamadı: şirket Ekim 2026'da 190 milyon Kanada dolarlık sermaye artırdı ve bundan sonraki bilançosu henüz yayımlanmadı; şirket zararda olduğu için 1. surda kalıyor.

Veri kaynağı 332 şirkette son 12 ayın kârını vermiyor. Piyasa değeri 80 milyon Kanada dolarının üstünde olanlar 27 şirket; en büyükleri Molson Coors Canada, Apotex, Baytex Energy, Vizsla Silver ve Hemlo Mining. Çoğu yeni kote olmuş ya da hesap dönemi değişmiş şirket. Bunların hepsi zararda değil (Molson Coors'un ana şirketi son 12 ayda kârda); kaynakta kâr verisi olmadığı için değerlendirilemediler ve sayfalarında 'kâr verisi eksik' yazar.

Kaynağın PD/DD alanı boş olan 46 şirkette PD/DD aynı kaynağın son bilanço alanlarından hesaplandı (34 şirkette son açıklanan, 12 şirkette son yıllık bilanço); hangisi olduğu şirketin sayfasında yazar.

Beş yıllık oranlar: stockanalysis.com oran sayfaları; 147 adayın hepsinin sayfası geldi. Kanada bankalarının mali yılı 31 Ekim'de biter; grafikte şirketin kendi mali yılları yazar, enflasyon düzeltmesi aynı adı taşıyan takvim yılının oranıyla yapılır. ABD dolarıyla raporlayan ya da başka ülkede çalışan şirketlerde de düzeltme Kanada enflasyonuyla yapıldı.

Yıl sonu enflasyonu: Kanada İstatistik Kurumu (Statistics Canada), tüketici fiyat endeksi, aralık ayı yıllık oranları (2021-2025). Son yıllık oran: Eylül 2026 (%3,1); ekim oranı 16 Kasım 2026'da açıklanacak.
2. suru geçen 8 şirketin hepsi okundu. Dördü 3. surda elendi: üçü kârı emtia fiyatına bağlı petrol ve maden şirketi (Hemisphere Energy, Alphamin, Steppe Gold), biri küçülen rehber işi (Yellow Pages).

en.inflation_note: Canadian companies do not apply inflation accounting. The return on equity of every company was therefore adjusted by year-end consumer inflation: 4.8% for 2021, 6.3% for 2022, 3.4% for 2023, 1.8% for 2024 and 2.4% for 2025. For the last 12 months the most recently published annual rate (September 2026, 3.1%) was used.
data_notes: Price, market value, P/E and P/B: TradingView screener, 13 November 2026. The universe is 2,440 stocks: 609 on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX), 1,249 on TSX Venture, 565 on the CSE and 17 on Cboe Canada. Exchange-traded funds and depositary receipts are not in the universe; the 52 real estate and investment trusts that are in it stay outside at Wall 1.

1,527 companies in the universe made a loss over the last 12 months; most are small mining exploration companies on TSX Venture and the CSE. This is not a data gap: according to TMX's August 2026 report, 59% of the 1,496 companies on TSX Venture are miners. Ten companies the source labels as loss-making were compared with a second source; all ten are loss-making. Of the 772 companies with a market value above 80 million Canadian dollars, 51% have a P/E.

For comparison: according to TMX's August 2026 report the TSX has 667 companies excluding funds and depositary receipts (609 in the universe, 9% fewer) and TSX Venture has 1,496 companies (1,249 in the universe, 17% fewer). The CSE reports 739 listed securities at 30 September 2026 (565 in the universe; the CSE counts securities, not companies). In total the universe is 16% below these numbers; the gap comes mostly from small stocks that do not trade. Because the gap is above 15%, and the other checks hold, the country is published with this note.

Checks (14 November 2026): for Royal Bank, TD, Bank of Montreal, Scotiabank and Enbridge the price agrees with a second source within 1%, market value within 4% and P/E within 1%; the P/B of the four banks equals the book value per share in their own third-quarter reports. The P/E calculated by the collector is 9.11 for Canadian Net REIT (9.10 with the company's reported profit). P/B is 1.096 for Brookfield Business Corporation (1.08 with equity at 30 September 2026) and 5.85 for Computer Modelling Group (5.74 with equity at 30 September 2026; the 3.8 on the ratio page rests on equity before the share buyback).

Corrected with the company's own document (14 November 2026). Brookfield Wealth Solutions: the P/E calculated by the collector (30.9) did not agree with a second source. The share is a class A share exchangeable into Brookfield Corporation, and only a very small part of profit is attributable to that class; P/E cannot be measured, so it was left empty and the company shows 'profit data missing'. The P/B of StrikePoint Gold (5.4) could not be confirmed: the company raised 190 million Canadian dollars in October 2026 and has not yet published a balance sheet after that; it is loss-making and stays at Wall 1.

For 332 companies the data source gives no profit figure for the last 12 months. 27 of them have a market value above 80 million Canadian dollars; the largest are Molson Coors Canada, Apotex, Baytex Energy, Vizsla Silver and Hemlo Mining. Most are newly listed or have changed their reporting period. Not all of them are loss-making (the parent of Molson Coors made a profit over the last 12 months); they could not be assessed because the source has no profit data, and their pages say 'profit data missing'.

For 46 companies where the source's P/B field is empty, P/B was calculated from the same source's latest balance-sheet fields (the latest reported balance sheet for 34 companies, the last annual balance sheet for 12); the company's page says which.

Five-year ratios: stockanalysis.com ratio pages; the pages of all 147 candidates arrived. Canadian banks end their fiscal year on 31 October; the chart shows each company's own fiscal years, and the inflation adjustment uses the rate of the calendar year with the same name. For companies that report in US dollars or operate in another country the adjustment was also made with Canadian inflation.
Year-end inflation: Statistics Canada, consumer price index, December annual rates (2021-2025). Latest annual rate: September 2026 (3.1%); the October rate is due on 16 November 2026.

All 8 companies that passed Wall 2 have been read. Four were eliminated at Wall 3: three are oil and mining companies whose profit depends on a commodity price (Hemisphere Energy, Alphamin, Steppe Gold), and one is a shrinking directory business (Yellow Pages).

HME.one: Küçük bir ağır petrol üreticisi. Hendek yok: fiyatı piyasa belirler. Hesaptaki pay yılda %19,6 büyüme varsayımına ve yüksek petrol fiyatına dayanıyor; 3. suru geçemedi.
HME.business: Hemisphere Energy, Kanada'da ağır petrol çıkarır ve satar. Üretimin %99'u ağır petroldür; şirket kuyulara polimer basarak eski sahalardan daha çok petrol alır. 2025'te günde ortalama 3.645 varil petrol eşdeğeri üretti; hasılat 93,9 milyon Kanada doları, net kâr 28,0 milyon dolar oldu. 2026'nın ilk yarısında üretim günde 3.693 varile, ortalama satış fiyatı varil başına 88,24 dolara geldi (geçen yıl 74,64).
HME.moat_text: Hendek yok; şirket 3. suru bu yüzden geçemedi. Petrol bir emtiadır: fiyatı şirket değil dünya piyasası belirler. Kanıt şirketin kendi beklentisinde: 2026 düzeltilmiş nakit akışı varil başına 60 ABD doları petrolde 40 milyon, 80 dolarda 57 milyon, 100 dolarda 78 milyon Kanada doları. Kâr da aynı yolu izledi: 2025'te satış fiyatı %11 düşünce net kâr 33,1 milyondan 28,0 milyon dolara indi; 2026'nın ikinci çeyreğinde fiyat 70,06 dolardan 103,18 dolara çıkınca kâr 7,1 milyondan 12,6 milyon dolara çıktı. Güçlü yanı düşük maliyet ve yavaş azalan üretim: işletme ve taşıma gideri varil başına yaklaşık 14-15 dolar, kanıtlanmış ve muhtemel rezerv 15,2 milyon varil (11,4 yıllık üretim). Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılın ortalamasında %36,4, en düşük yılında %22,2; ama bu beş yıl petrol döngüsünün iyi yıllarıdır, tam bir döngüyü göstermez.
HME.mgmt: Banka borcu yok; 30 Haziran 2026'da işletme sermayesi 19,5 milyon dolar. Kâr ortaklara dönüyor: 2025'te 9,6 milyon dolar olağan ve 5,8 milyon dolar özel temettü ödendi, 3,5 milyon pay ortalama 1,88 dolardan geri alındı. 2026'nın ilk yarısında 10,4 milyon dolar temettü ödendi (ikinci çeyrekte hisse başına 0,06 dolar özel temettü dahil); ikinci çeyrekte 30.000 pay 2,52 dolardan geri alındı. Pay sayısı 2024 sonundaki 97,4 milyondan 94,5 milyona indi; 4,1 milyon opsiyon duruyor (payların %4,4'ü). Kaynak beş yılda %10,8 pay artışı gösteriyor; bu artış ilk yıllara ait, son üç yılda pay sayısı azaldı. Hisse bazlı ücret tutarı, şerefiye, kuyu terk yükümlülüğü ve ilişkili taraf işlemleri: bakıldı, okunan bültenlerde yok (finansal tablo dipnotları açılmadı). Hâkim ortak bilgisi: bakıldı, okunan belgelerde yok.
HME.latest: 20 Ağustos 2026: Şirket ikinci çeyrek sonuçlarını açıkladı. Üretim günde 3.576 varil (geçen yıl 3.826), satış fiyatı varil başına 103,18 dolar (70,06), hasılat 33,6 milyon dolar (24,4 milyon), net kâr 12,6 milyon dolar (7,1 milyon), hisse başına kâr 0,13 dolar (0,07). İlk yarıda net kâr 20,4 milyon dolar (16,0 milyon), seyreltilmiş hisse başına kâr 0,21 dolar (0,16). İlk çeyrekte kâr geçen yılın altındaydı (7,9 milyon; 8,9 milyon). Şirket üretimini fiyata karşı korumuyor (hedge yok). Atlee Buffalo'da dokuza kadar yeni kuyu planlanıyor; Marsden'deki polimer denemesinden henüz sınırlı sonuç alındı.
risks: Hesaptaki güvenlik marjı yılda %19,6 reel büyüme varsayımına ve petrolün bugünkü yüksek fiyatına dayanıyor. Üretim büyümüyor (2026'nın ikinci çeyreğinde geçen yıla göre %6,5 düşük); kârdaki artış fiyattan geliyor. Fiyat düşerse kâr da düşer: şirketin kendi tablosunda 60 dolarlık petrolde nakit akışı 80 dolardakinin %30 altında.

Beş yıllık geçmiş petrol döngüsünün yalnız iyi bölümünü gösteriyor; döngünün neresinde olunduğu bilinmiyor. İkinci çeyrekte varil başına 103 dolarlık satış fiyatı 2025 ortalamasının (70,56) %46 üstünde.
Tek ürün, tek bölge: üretimin %99'u ağır petrol. Kanada ağır petrolünün indirimi (WCS farkı) ve boru hattı kapasitesi fiyatı ayrıca etkiler.
Rezerv sınırlı: üretimdeki kanıtlanmış rezervler 7,0 yıllık. Yeni saha (Marsden) henüz kendini kanıtlamadı.
Kraliyet payı (royalty) ve vergi fiyatla birlikte artar: ikinci çeyrekte kraliyet payı varil başına 13,11 dolardan 20,73 dolara çıktı.

en.one: A small heavy oil producer. No moat: the market sets its price. The margin in the calculation rests on an assumed 19.6% yearly growth and a high oil price; it did not pass wall 3.
en.business: Hemisphere Energy produces and sells heavy oil in Canada. Heavy oil is 99% of output; the company injects polymer into wells to recover more oil from old fields. In 2025 it produced an average of 3,645 barrels of oil equivalent a day; revenue was 93.9 million Canadian dollars and net income 28.0 million dollars. In the first half of 2026 production was 3,693 barrels a day and the average realised price 88.24 dollars a barrel (74.64 a year earlier).
en.moat_text: There is no moat; this is why the company did not pass wall 3. Oil is a commodity: the world market sets the price, not the company. The evidence is in the company's own guidance: 2026 adjusted funds flow is 40 million Canadian dollars at 60 US dollars a barrel, 57 million at 80 dollars and 78 million at 100 dollars. Profit followed the same path: in 2025 the realised price fell 11% and net income fell from 33.1 million to 28.0 million dollars; in the second quarter of 2026 the price rose from 70.06 to 103.18 dollars and profit rose from 7.1 million to 12.6 million dollars. Its strengths are low cost and slowly declining production: operating and transport costs are about 14-15 dollars a barrel, and proved plus probable reserves are 15.2 million barrels (11.4 years of production). Real return on equity averaged 36.4% over five years and was 22.2% in the weakest year; but these five years are the good years of the oil cycle and do not show a full cycle.
en.mgmt: There is no bank debt; working capital was 19.5 million dollars on 30 June 2026. Profit goes back to shareholders: in 2025 the company paid 9.6 million dollars in base dividends and 5.8 million in special dividends, and bought back 3.5 million shares at an average of 1.88 dollars. In the first half of 2026 it paid 10.4 million dollars in dividends (including a special dividend of 0.06 dollars a share in the second quarter); in the second quarter it bought back 30,000 shares at 2.52 dollars. The share count fell from 97.4 million at the end of 2024 to 94.5 million; 4.1 million options are outstanding (4.4% of shares). The data source shows a 10.8% rise in the share count over five years; that rise belongs to the early years, and the count has fallen in the last three. Share-based pay, goodwill, well abandonment obligations and related-party transactions: checked, not in the releases read (the notes to the financial statements were not opened). Controlling shareholder: checked, not in the documents read.
en.latest: 20 August 2026: The company reported second quarter results. Production was 3,576 barrels a day (3,826 a year earlier), the realised price 103.18 dollars a barrel (70.06), revenue 33.6 million dollars (24.4 million), net income 12.6 million dollars (7.1 million) and earnings per share 0.13 dollars (0.07). First-half net income was 20.4 million dollars (16.0 million) and diluted earnings per share 0.21 dollars (0.16). In the first quarter profit was below last year (7.9 million; 8.9 million). The company does not hedge its production. Up to nine new wells are planned at Atlee Buffalo; the polymer pilot at Marsden has shown only a limited response so far.
risks: The margin of safety in the calculation rests on an assumed real growth of 19.6% a year and on today's high oil price. Production is not growing (6.5% below last year in the second quarter of 2026); the rise in profit comes from price. If the price falls, profit falls: in the company's own table, funds flow at 60 dollar oil is 30% below that at 80 dollars.
The five-year history shows only the good part of the oil cycle; where we are in the cycle is unknown. The second-quarter realised price of 103 dollars a barrel is 46% above the 2025 average (70.56).
One product, one region: 99% of output is heavy oil. The discount on Canadian heavy oil (the WCS differential) and pipeline capacity also move the price.
Reserves are limited: proved developed producing reserves cover 7.0 years. The new area (Marsden) has not proved itself yet.
Royalties and taxes rise with the price: royalties rose from 13.11 to 20.73 dollars a barrel in the second quarter.

AFM.one: Kongo'da tek bir kalay madeni işletir. Maden çok zengin ve ucuz üretir; ama kalay bir emtiadır ve her şey tek madene bağlıdır. 3. suru geçemedi.
AFM.business: Alphamin, Kongo Demokratik Cumhuriyeti'nin Kuzey Kivu bölgesindeki Bisie kalay madenini işletir ve kalay konsantresi satar. Madenin %84,14'ü şirketin; %5'i Kongo devletinin, %10,86'sı IDC'nin. Yılda yaklaşık 20.000 ton kalay üretir. 2025'te hasılat 620,9 milyon ABD doları, ana ortaklık kârı 148,0 milyon dolar oldu. Şirket dolarla raporlar; hisse Kanada'da ve Johannesburg'da işlem görür.
AFM.moat_text: Hendek yok; şirket 3. suru bu yüzden geçemedi. Kalay bir emtiadır: fiyatı dünya piyasası belirler, şirket belirlemez. Güçlü yanı gerçek: işlenen cevherin kalay oranı %3,2-3,3 ve 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde ton başına toplam maliyet 20.642 dolar, satış fiyatı 54.374 dolar. Bu bir maliyet üstünlüğüdür; ama tek bir madene bağlıdır ve o madenin ömrü sınırlıdır (kapanış karşılığı dokuz yıllık kalan ömür varsayar). Kâr fiyatla oynar: reel özsermaye kârlılığı 2023'te %12,0'ye indi, son 12 ayda %53,7. Dayanıklılık puanı sıfır: maden silahlı çatışma bölgesinde. 13 Mart 2025'te güvenlik nedeniyle boşaltıldı, 9 Nisan 2025'te yeniden açıldı.
AFM.mgmt: Hâkim ortak International Resources Holding (IRH): 22 Temmuz 2025'te Tremont'un %56 payını hisse başına 0,70 Kanada dolarından aldı. Kârın neredeyse tamamı dağıtılıyor: kaynağa göre dağıtım oranı %101. 5 Haziran 2026'da hisse başına 0,13 Kanada doları (121 milyon ABD doları) ve 6 Kasım 2026'da yine 0,13 Kanada doları (yaklaşık 120 milyon ABD doları) temettü ödendi. 30 Eylül 2026'da net nakit 199,8 milyon dolar. Kontrol değişikliği yüzünden Kongo vergi idaresi 32 milyon dolar ve ceza tutarında değer artış vergisi istedi; şirket dava açtı. 2026'nın ilk yarısında 17,0 milyon dolar ek 'aşırı kâr vergisi' yazıldı. en.one: It runs a single tin mine in DR Congo. The mine is very rich and produces cheaply; but tin is a commodity and everything depends on one mine. It did not pass wall 3.
en.business: Alphamin operates the Bisie tin mine in the North Kivu region of the Democratic Republic of Congo and sells tin concentrate. The company owns 84.14% of the mine; the DRC government holds 5% and IDC 10.86%. It produces about 20,000 tonnes of tin a year. In 2025 revenue was 620.9 million US dollars and profit attributable to shareholders 148.0 million dollars. The company reports in dollars; the shares trade in Canada and Johannesburg.
en.moat_text: There is no moat; this is why the company did not pass wall 3. Tin is a commodity: the world market sets the price, not the company. Its strength is real: the ore processed grades 3.2-3.3% tin, and in the third quarter of 2026 the all-in cost was 20,642 dollars a tonne against a selling price of 54,374 dollars. That is a cost advantage; but it rests on a single mine with a limited life (the closure provision assumes nine years of remaining life). Profit moves with the price: real return on equity fell to 12.0% in 2023 and is 53.7% over the last 12 months. The resilience score is zero: the mine is in an armed conflict zone. It was evacuated for security reasons on 13 March 2025 and reopened on 9 April 2025.
en.mgmt: The controlling shareholder is International Resources Holding (IRH): on 22 July 2025 it bought Tremont's 56% stake at 0.70 Canadian dollars a share. Almost all profit is paid out: the payout ratio is 101% according to the data source. A dividend of 0.13 Canadian dollars a share (121 million US dollars) was paid on 5 June 2026 and another 0.13 Canadian dollars (about 120 million US dollars) on 6 November 2026. Net cash was 199.8 million dollars on 30 September 2026. Because of the change of control the DRC tax authority assessed a capital gains tax of 32 million dollars plus penalties; the company is challenging it in court. An extra 'super profit tax' of 17.0 million dollars was booked in the first half of 2026. The data source shows a 20.9% rise in the share count over five years; the rise belongs to the first year. Share-based pay, goodwill and pension obligations: checked, no material amount in the documents read. There are no buybacks.
en.latest: 6 October 2026: The company gave preliminary third quarter figures. Production was 5,030 tonnes of tin (5,013 in the second quarter), sales 5,046 tonnes, the average price 54,374 dollars a tonne (51,957), EBITDA guidance 171 million dollars (167 million) and all-in cost 20,642 dollars a tonne (19,042; diesel and transport cost more). The third quarter financial statements were published on 13 November 2026; they could not be opened while this report was written. In the first half of 2026 profit attributable to shareholders was 127.7 million dollars (55.4 million a year earlier) and diluted earnings per share 9.95 cents (4.30). Last year's first half includes the four weeks when the mine was shut.
risks: Everything depends on one mine and one country. The mine is in eastern Congo, in an armed conflict zone; it was evacuated for four weeks in March 2025. Another shutdown would stop the profit.
Profit depends on the tin price, and the price is high today: 54,374 dollars a tonne in the third quarter. Five years do not show a full cycle; real return on equity fell to 12.0% in 2023.
The tax burden in Congo is rising: the super profit tax lifts the rate on profit above the threshold from 30% to 50%; the 32 million dollar capital gains tax case is still open.
The remaining mine life is short (nine years in the closure provision). A new resource estimate is expected in the last quarter of 2026.
The company operates in Congo and reports in dollars; the inflation adjustment here uses Canadian inflation. The shares trade in Canadian dollars, so the exchange rate also moves the price.

en.business: Steppe Gold operates the ATO gold mine in Mongolia and sells gold. In 2025 it produced 76,059 ounces of gold; revenue was 254.1 million US dollars and net income 32.8 million dollars. en.moat_text: There is no moat; this is why the company did not pass wall 3. Gold is a commodity and the company does not set its price. The rise in profit comes from price: in the second quarter of 2026 the realised price was 4,493 dollars an ounce, against 2,142 dollars a year earlier (when sales were tied to a fixed-price contract at 2,000 dollars). The balance sheet holds 107.1 million dollars of bond investments maturing on 31 December 2026; the release does not name the issuer. In the past year the auditor changed (December 2025) and changes in senior and finance leadership were announced (December 2025, February 2026). en.one: The grocer of remote communities in northern Canada, Alaska and the islands. The moat is narrow but real; profit has not grown in real terms for five years, and it failed the retained-earnings test.
en.business: North West Company sells food and everyday goods in small communities that are not connected by road. It has 230 stores: Northern and NorthMart in Canada, Alaska Commercial in Alaska, Cost-U-Less and RiteWay on Pacific and Caribbean islands. About 77% of sales are food. It moves goods with its own airline (North Star Air, 19 aircraft) and a shipping company it half owns. In the fiscal year ended 31 January 2026 sales were 2,598 million Canadian dollars and profit attributable to shareholders 139.5 million dollars; 56.5% of sales came from Canada.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from location and logistics: 115 of the Canadian stores cannot be reached by all-weather roads, and every Alaska store is supplied by air or water. These communities of 200 to 8,500 people cannot support a second large store. The company says it is the leading provider in most of the communities it serves; it gives no market share figure. The evidence of pricing power is the gross profit rate: 32.8% in 2021, 31.8% in 2022 when inflation rose (the company said it could not fully pass on higher freight and merchandise costs), 32.7% in 2023, 33.7% in 2024 and 33.9% in 2025. So the rate slipped for one year, then rose above its old level. The weak side: customers' income depends largely on government payments; competitors are local co-operatives and independent stores, plus online ordering (Amazon, Walmart, Costco). Real return on equity fell from 21.4% to 14.4% over five years; the average is 16.8%.
en.mgmt: There is no controlling shareholder; variable voting shares held by non-Canadians are 33.0% of the total. About 55% of profit goes to dividends: 1.62 dollars a share in fiscal 2025 (77.5 million dollars); the quarterly dividend rose to 0.42 dollars in September 2026. In the same year 309,564 shares were bought back for 15.0 million dollars (an average of 48.45 dollars by our arithmetic); there were no buybacks in the first quarter of 2026. The rest of the profit is invested in the business: 137.8 million dollars in 2025 and about 150 million planned for 2026 (store renovations, aircraft purchases). But real earnings per share did not grow in five years (2021: 3.16 dollars, 2025: 2.87 dollars); on this measure retained profit did not earn the required return, which is why the D score is 1. Total debt is 311.4 million dollars and debt to equity 0.38. Share-based pay was 12.7 million dollars in 2025 (pre-tax; about 9% of net earnings). The company's 'adjusted' earnings leave out this expense and the costs the 'Next 100' programme calls one-time; those costs recurred in 2024, 2025 and 2026, and we treat them as ordinary. Goodwill is 51.2 million dollars (6% of equity). The pension plans are in surplus; the obligation is 19.5 million dollars. A 12.5 million dollar receivable from Giant Tiger is past due and in litigation. Related-party transactions: checked, not in the documents read.
en.latest: 8 September 2026: The company reported the second quarter ended 31 July 2026. Sales were 682.0 million dollars (+5.4%), same-store sales +6.7% (−1.1% a year earlier), EBITDA 89.8 million dollars (85.2 million), net earnings 38.3 million dollars (+1.9%), earnings attributable to shareholders 36.8 million dollars and diluted earnings per share 0.76 dollars (0.74). Profit includes a 2.4 million dollar gain (1.7 million after tax) on an asset sale; the first quarter also included a 3.8 million dollar gain (3.0 million after tax) on the sale of a store in Guam. Fuel-related freight costs rose; the company said it passed them through without adding a markup. First Nations child welfare settlement payments increased late in the quarter; the company expects them to continue in the second half of 2026 and for several years.
risks: It failed the retained-earnings test: the company keeps about 42% of its profit, but real earnings per share did not grow in five years. The measure starts from the high profit of the pandemic year 2021; even so, the new investment (about 150 million dollars a year) has not yet been seen to lift profit.

The last 12 months' profit includes two gains on asset sales (4.7 million dollars after tax in total; 3.3% of profit). They do not recur; most of the 3.9% rise in first-half earnings per share comes from them.

Customers' income depends on government payments. In 2025 the food voucher programme for Inuit children was eliminated and Canadian same-store sales fell 1.0%. Settlement payments lift sales for a time; sales fall back when they end.
Fuel and freight costs weigh more than at other retailers. They cut the gross profit rate by one point in 2022; fuel became more expensive again in 2026.
Share-based pay is about 9% of net earnings; the company's adjusted earnings do not count it.

43.5% of sales come from outside Canada (Alaska, the Caribbean, the Pacific); the inflation adjustment here uses Canadian inflation only. The Caribbean stores carry hurricane risk (sales in that region are 443.4 million dollars).

en.one: Canadian supplier of video and audio infrastructure to broadcasters. It passed the quality criteria, but profit fell last quarter and the dividend exceeds earnings.
en.business: Evertz sells video and audio infrastructure to television broadcasters, telecom companies and new-media companies: routers, monitoring and playout systems and the software that runs them. In the fiscal year ended 30 April 2026 revenue was 515.8 million Canadian dollars: 275.1 million from hardware and 240.7 million from recurring software, services and other (47%). The company says about 65-75% of its revenue comes from the United States and Canada. It has a single operating segment.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The evidence is in the margin: gross margin was 59.5% in fiscal 2025 and 59.3% in fiscal 2026, and stayed between 57.8% and 61.7% in the six quarters we read. The company spends about 29% of revenue on research and development (148.1 million dollars in fiscal 2026); a rival would need years to build the same product range. Recurring software and services revenue rose from 222.6 million to 240.7 million dollars in a year. Real return on equity averaged 22% over five years and was 19% in its lowest year, with no bank debt. The weak side: the documents we read give no market share figure. Much of the business is project-based, order-driven hardware sales that swing from quarter to quarter. The trend in real earnings per share over the last five fiscal years is negative. In the July 2026 quarter gross margin fell from 61.4% to 58.6%.
en.mgmt: The founding shareholders run the company; ownership percentages are not in the documents we read (checked). The company rents some of its buildings from entities in which its shareholders hold indirect interests: rent paid in fiscal 2026 was about 3.6 million dollars. More than all of the profit goes to shareholders: 136.7 million dollars of dividends were paid in fiscal 2026 (75.5 million of it a special dividend of 1.00 dollar per share), against net earnings of 64.0 million dollars. The regular dividend is 0.205 dollars a quarter, 0.82 dollars a year; earnings per share for the last 12 months were 0.78 dollars. Cash was 111.7 million dollars on 30 April 2025; on 31 July 2026 it was 2.5 million dollars net of bank indebtedness. Buybacks are small: 343,335 shares in fiscal 2026 at an average of 11.92 dollars. Share-based compensation was 6.0 million dollars, 9% of net earnings. Goodwill is 32.2 million dollars, 16% of equity. No pension obligation appears in the documents (checked). Letters of credit total 13.3 million dollars.
en.latest: 14 September 2026: The company reported the quarter ended 31 July 2026 (first quarter of fiscal 2027). Revenue was 118.3 million dollars (112.1 a year earlier; +5.5%). Gross margin was 58.6% (61.4%). Net earnings attributable to shareholders were 7.8 million dollars (11.8 million; −34%); diluted earnings per share were 0.10 dollars (0.15). The reasons for the fall: lower gross margin, share-based compensation of 2.4 million dollars (1.1) and a foreign exchange loss of 0.5 million dollars (a gain of 0.7 million a year earlier). Cash from operations was 0.8 million dollars (33.5); inventory rose from 200.2 million to 215.1 million dollars. At the end of August the order backlog was above 259 million dollars. The quarterly dividend is 0.205 dollars.
risks: The regular dividend (0.82 dollars a year) exceeds earnings per share for the last 12 months (0.78 dollars); after the special dividend cash is down to 2.5 million dollars. If profit does not recover, the dividend will be paid with debt or cut.
Profit is falling: earnings per share dropped from 0.15 to 0.10 dollars in the latest quarter. The real profit trend over the last five fiscal years is also negative.

Customers are broadcasters and media companies; their capital budgets are cyclical and the timing of large projects moves quarterly results. The share of the largest customers is not in the documents we read (checked).
Share-based compensation equals 9% of net earnings and is rising (2.4 million dollars in the latest quarter; 1.1 a year earlier).
Most revenue is in US dollars while a large part of costs is in Canadian dollars; the exchange rate moves profit. The company rents buildings from parties related to its shareholders.

The evidence: 73% of revenue is licences renewed every year; gross margin is about 82% (fiscal 2026; our calculation). Real return on equity averaged 28% over five years; the lowest reading is 15% (last 12 months). No customer exceeds 10% of revenue. The weak side is starting to weigh more: real return on equity fell from 41% in fiscal 2024 to 15%. In fiscal 2026 revenue excluding acquisitions fell 13%; a single contract loss pulled recurring revenue down. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 34% in fiscal 2025, 29% in fiscal 2026 and 22% in the latest half-year. The acquired seismic software businesses earn lower margins than the core. The durability of the moat is uncertain.
en.mgmt: No controlling shareholder appears in the documents we read (checked). Since 2023 management has directed profit to acquisitions: the quarterly dividend was cut from 0.05 to 0.01 dollars in August 2025, which the company says frees about 13 million dollars a year. It paid 17.3 million dollars in cash for SeisWare and Rose. Then the direction changed: in September 2026 the company bought back 4,444,444 shares at 4.50 dollars (20.0 million dollars) and paid for it from its credit facility; it also bought and cancelled 4,760,700 shares on the market. In six months it spent 22.3 million dollars on buybacks and 5.4 million on shares for the employee plan; net income in the same period was 2.0 million dollars. Equity fell from 78.3 million dollars on 31 March 2026 to 53.3 million. Credit facility debt is 29.9 million dollars; cash is 9.3 million. Goodwill and intangible assets are 91.2 million dollars, 1.7 times equity. Share-based compensation is small (0.5 million dollars in fiscal 2026). Acquisition costs recur every year (2.6 and 1.0 million dollars); we treat them as ordinary costs. In the latest quarter the company made about 1.0 million dollars of unauthorised payments in a fraud. No pension obligation appears in the sections we read (checked).
en.latest: 12 November 2026: The company reported the quarter ended 30 September 2026 (second quarter of fiscal 2027). Revenue was 29.3 million dollars (30.2 a year earlier; −3%); recurring revenue was 22.1 million (+7%) and professional services 5.9 million (8.5). Total revenue excluding acquisitions fell 10%. Net income was 0.7 million dollars (2.7 million; −74%); earnings per share were 0.01 dollars (0.03). For six months net income was 2.0 million dollars (6.0) and earnings per share 0.03 dollars (0.07). A fraud loss of 0.8 million dollars was booked in the quarter. The company's outlook for fiscal 2027: professional services revenue will fall by 6-7 million dollars, recurring revenue excluding acquisitions will be stable, and adjusted EBITDA will not decline. The credit facility was raised to 150 million dollars on 9 October 2026.
risks: Profit is falling fast: net income for the last 12 months is 13.4 million dollars, against 22.4 million in fiscal 2025. In the last six months net income fell 66%. A price calculation that rests on past profitability looks better than it should.
The company spent far more than its profit on buybacks and paid for them with debt; equity shrank by a third in six months. The buyback price (4.50 dollars) is above our conservative value.
Growth depends on acquisitions; the acquired businesses earn lower margins, and goodwill and intangible assets are 1.7 times equity. An impairment would shrink equity further.
Customers are oil and gas companies; their software budgets depend on the oil price and on mergers in the industry. Three customers make up 36% of trade receivables.
The largest renewal quarter is the fourth (January-March); weak renewals would leave the year's profit below the outlook.

OLY.one: Özel şirket payı ve ipotek tutan emeklilik hesaplarını yöneten Kanadalı emanet şirketi. Kalite ölçütlerini geçti; ama kârının yarısı faize bağlı ve kâr düşüyor.
OLY.business: Olympia Financial Group, bağlı şirketi Olympia Trust Company ile bireylerin vergi avantajlı tasarruf hesaplarını yönetir; bu hesaplar borsada işlem görmeyen şirket payları ve ipotek alacakları tutar. Şirket iki yoldan para kazanır: hesap ve işlem ücretleri, bir de müşterilerin emanetteki nakdinden elde edilen faiz. 2025'te hasılat 98,9 milyon Kanada doları: 50,0 milyonu hizmet geliri, 48,9 milyonu emanet ve faiz geliri. Net kârın neredeyse tamamı (19,6 milyon dolar) yatırım hesapları bölümünden geldi. Bu bölümde emanetteki varlıklar 2025 sonunda 11,66 milyar dolar özel menkul kıymet ve ipotek, 1,19 milyar dolar nakit ve borsa hissesi. Şirket ayrıca işverenlere özel sağlık harcama planı ve şirketlere pay kayıt hizmeti verir.
OLY.moat_text: Hendek dar. Üstünlük lisanstan ve küçük bir alandaki ölçekten geliyor: özel menkul kıymet tutan hesapları yönetmek emanet şirketi lisansı ister ve büyük bankalar bu işi yapmıyor. Şirket, bu alana başkalarının girmekte zorlandığını ve rakiplerin hesaplarını zamanla kendisinin devraldığını söylüyor; 2025 başında Canadian Western Trust'tan yaklaşık 3.400 hesap aldı. Fiyatlama gücünün işareti: faiz geliri düşerken hizmet geliri aylık ücret ve işlem ücreti artışıyla büyüdü (2026'nın ilk dokuz ayında +%2, 2025'te +%5). Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılın ortalamasında %48, en düşük yılında %28; son 12 ayda %31. Zayıf yanı: pazar payı rakamı yok. Kârın büyük bölümü şirketin denetiminde olmayan faiz oranına bağlı: şirketin hesabına göre faizdeki 1 puanlık düşüş vergi sonrası kârı yaklaşık 11,1 milyon dolar azaltır; 2025 net kârı 19,9 milyon dolardı. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı 2023'teki %73'ten %31'e indi.
OLY.mgmt: Genel müdür payların %29,62'sini elinde tutuyor (Şubat 2026). Yönetim düzeni küçük ortak açısından kusurlu: şirket, genel müdürün denetimindeki Tarman ATM'ye bölüm kârlarının bir yüzdesi olarak yönetim ücreti ödüyor (2025'te 9,04 milyon dolar); şirketin örnek hesabına göre yöneticilere 2025'te toplam 18,4 milyon dolar gitti. 15 Temmuz 2026'da şirket bu sözleşmeleri sona erdirmek için anlaştı: Tarman ve üç yöneticiye yaklaşık 44,9 milyon dolar nakit ve 433.493 yeni pay verilecek (toplam değer 49,7 milyon dolar); nakit yeni bir krediyle ödenecek. Şirket, sonrasında yönetici ücretinin yılda 2,9-4,0 milyon dolara ineceğini söylüyor. İşlem ilişkili taraf işlemidir; bağımsız üyelerden oluşan komite inceledi, bağımsız değerleme alındı, ortaklar 24 Ağustos 2026'da onayladı, mahkeme onayı çıktı. 27 Ağustos 2026'da kredi ve Alberta Maliye Bakanı'nın onayı bekleniyordu; kapanış duyurusu bulunamadı. Kârın çoğu temettüye gidiyor (2025'te hisse başına 7,20 dolar; kâr 8,25). Aylık temettü Mayıs 2026'da 0,60 dolardan 0,50 dolara indirildi. Geri alım yok. 2025 sonunda kredi borcu sıfır. Şirket 2026'da iki zarar eden işi sattı: döviz ve ödeme şirketi (Nisan) ve Raisr (Temmuz). Hisse bazlı ücret ve şerefiye belgede yok (bakıldı); maddi olmayan varlıklar 4,0 milyon dolar.
OLY.latest: 13 Kasım 2026: Şirket 2026'nın ilk dokuz ayını açıkladı. Süren faaliyetlerden net kâr 13,43 milyon dolar (bir yıl önce 16,13 milyon; −%17); hisse başına kâr 5,58 dolar (6,70). Kârın içinde 3,99 milyon dolarlık diğer kazanç var; büyük bölümü Raisr bölümünün satışından geliyor. Giderler %2 arttı (50,10 milyon dolar): risk ve uyum kadroları büyüdü, Calgary'deki yeni merkez binanın kirası başladı. İlk yarıda net kâr 7,06 milyon dolardı (11,25 milyon; −%37).

en.one: Canadian trust company that administers retirement accounts holding private company shares and mortgages. It passed the quality criteria, but half its profit depends on interest rates and profit is falling.
en.business: Olympia Financial Group, through its subsidiary Olympia Trust Company, administers individuals' tax-advantaged savings accounts that hold shares of unlisted companies and mortgage loans. It earns money in two ways: account and transaction fees, and interest on clients' cash held in trust. In 2025 revenue was 98.9 million Canadian dollars: 50.0 million of service revenue and 48.9 million of trust and interest income. Almost all net earnings (19.6 million dollars) came from the investment accounts division. Assets held in trust in that division at the end of 2025 were 11.66 billion dollars of private securities and mortgages and 1.19 billion dollars of cash and listed securities. The company also offers private health spending plans to employers and share registry services to companies.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from a licence and from scale in a small niche: administering accounts that hold private securities requires a trust company licence, and the large banks do not do this work. The company says others have found the field hard to enter and that it has taken over competitors' accounts over time; at the start of 2025 it acquired about 3,400 accounts from Canadian Western Trust. A sign of pricing power: while interest income fell, service revenue grew through higher monthly and transaction fees (+2% in the first nine months of 2026, +5% in 2025). Real return on equity averaged 48% over five years and was 28% in its lowest year; it is 31% for the last 12 months. The weak side: there is no market share figure. A large part of profit depends on interest rates, which the company does not control: by its own calculation a 1 point fall in rates lowers after-tax earnings by about 11.1 million dollars; 2025 net earnings were 19.9 million dollars. Real return on equity has fallen from 73% in 2023 to 31%.
en.mgmt: The chief executive holds 29.62% of the shares (February 2026). The management set-up is flawed from a minority shareholder's view: the company pays management fees, set as a percentage of divisional profits, to Tarman ATM, which the chief executive controls (9.04 million dollars in 2025); by the company's illustrative figure, executives received 18.4 million dollars in total in 2025. On 15 July 2026 the company agreed to end these contracts: Tarman and three executives will receive about 44.9 million dollars in cash and 433,493 new shares (49.7 million dollars in total value); the cash will be paid with a new loan. The company says executive pay will then fall to 2.9-4.0 million dollars a year. This is a related-party transaction; a committee of independent directors reviewed it, an independent valuation was obtained, shareholders approved it on 24 August 2026 and the court order was granted. On 27 August 2026 the loan and the approval of Alberta's Minister of Finance were still awaited; we found no closing announcement. Most profit goes to dividends (7.20 dollars per share in 2025; earnings 8.25). The monthly dividend was cut from 0.60 to 0.50 dollars in May 2026. There are no buybacks. Credit facility debt was nil at the end of 2025. In 2026 the company sold two loss-making businesses: the currency and payments company (April) and Raisr (July). Share-based compensation and goodwill do not appear in the document (checked); intangible assets are 4.0 million dollars.
en.latest: 13 November 2026: The company reported the first nine months of 2026. Net earnings from continuing operations were 13.43 million dollars (16.13 million a year earlier; −17%); earnings per share were 5.58 dollars (6.70). Revenue was 64.16 million dollars (−9%): service revenue 34.04 million (+2%), trust and interest income 30.12 million (−19%). The company attributes the fall to lower interest rates on funds held in trust. Profit includes other gains of 3.99 million dollars, most of it from the sale of the Raisr division. Expenses rose 2% (50.10 million dollars): risk and compliance teams grew and the lease on the new Calgary head office began. In the first half net earnings were 7.06 million dollars (11.25 million; −37%).
risks: Half of profit depends on interest rates, and rates are falling: trust and interest income dropped 19% in the first nine months. By the company's calculation a 1 point fall in rates lowers after-tax earnings by about 11.1 million dollars.
Recent profit is supported by a one-off gain: 3.99 million of the nine-month pre-tax profit (18.05 million dollars) is a gain on sale. Without it the fall is larger than 17%.

Ending the management contracts will cost 49.7 million dollars paid to related parties: 44.9 million with debt and the rest with new shares that raise the share count by about 18%. A debt-free company will borrow; equity was 44.4 million dollars at the end of 2025. The effect on the statements has not yet been disclosed.

The business depends on its licence and its regulators: the company plans to become a federal trust company so that it can serve clients in Ontario, where a significant share of its investment accounts are. Delay or extra capital requirements would affect profit.
If the private securities and mortgages held by clients lose value, account numbers and fee income would fall; the company is party to various legal actions (it expects no significant effect).

Y.business: Yellow Pages, Kanada'daki küçük işletmelere reklam ve dijital pazarlama hizmeti satar: basılı rehberler, YP.ca ve bağlı siteler, internet sitesi yapımı, arama motoru reklamı. 2025'te hasılat 198,9 milyon Kanada doları: 161,3 milyonu dijital, 37,6 milyonu basılı. Y.moat_text: Hendek zayıf; şirket 3. suru burada geçemedi. en.one: Canada's directory and local advertising company. It did not pass the moat criterion: revenue shrinks 7-10% every year and the customer count is falling.
en.business: Yellow Pages sells advertising and digital marketing services to small businesses in Canada: print directories, YP.ca and related sites, website building and search engine advertising. In 2025 revenue was 198.9 million Canadian dollars: 161.3 million digital and 37.6 million print. Adjusted EBITDA was 43.0 million dollars (21.6% of revenue) and net income 18.1 million dollars.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is where the company failed wall 3. It has a known brand and a wide sales network, but the business is shrinking structurally: total revenue fell 10.3% in 2024, 7.4% in 2025 and 7.6% in the first nine months of 2026. Not only print but digital revenue is declining too (6.3% in 2025; 6.3% in the latest quarter). The company attributes the fall to a lower digital customer count; spend per customer is rising but does not make up the loss. It can raise prices on the print product, which shows some pricing power with the customers who remain; but the customer base is eroding. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.7% in 2024, 21.6% in 2025 and 19.1% in the first nine months of 2026. Real return on equity is high (41% for the last 12 months; 31% at its five-year low) because the business needs very little capital and equity has been shrunk by buybacks. High profitability here shows the cash harvest of a shrinking business, not a lasting advantage.
en.mgmt: Management returns the cash of a shrinking business to shareholders, which is consistent capital allocation. There is no bank debt; cash was about 49 million dollars at the end of October 2026 (64 million at the end of January 2026). The quarterly dividend is 0.25 dollars per share. The share count has fallen through buybacks: earnings per share rose 21% in nine months while net income rose 14%; the amount and price of the buybacks are not in the documents we read (checked). The company makes voluntary extra payments into its pension plan: the last 2.0 million of a 4.0 million dollar contribution announced in May 2025 was paid in the first quarter of 2026. Restructuring charges recur every year; we treat them as ordinary costs. A controlling shareholder, the amount of share-based compensation and goodwill do not appear in the documents we read (checked).
en.latest: 12 November 2026: The company reported its third quarter. Revenue was 45.0 million dollars (48.3 a year earlier; −7.0%): digital revenue fell 6.3% and print revenue 9.9%. Adjusted EBITDA was 8.5 million dollars (10.0; −15%) and the margin 18.8% (20.6%). Net income was 4.6 million dollars (4.0); earnings per share were 0.40 dollars (0.30). Net income rose thanks to a net recovery in restructuring and other charges; the amount is not in the release. For nine months revenue was 139.4 million dollars (150.8), net income 12.0 million dollars (10.6) and diluted earnings per share 0.92 dollars (0.76). The company says revenue pressure and product mix will continue to weigh on margins in the coming quarters. It launched an AI-powered phone receptionist product.
risks: Revenue shrinks 7-10% every year and the company says margin pressure will continue; adjusted EBITDA fell 18% in nine months.
The pension plan obligation remains; the company makes voluntary extra payments. The size of the deficit is not in the documents we read (checked).
